newsitem.title: CHILE: LatAm shares seen sluggish, looking to Wall Street.
newsitem.headline: LatAm shares seen sluggish, looking to Wall Street.

text.p: Investors can expect a quiet week as most Latin American markets are seen drifting sideways or lower, with players keeping a close eye on the U.S. Federal Reserve's meeting Wednesday, said dealers.

Stocks are seen taking their cue from Wall Street with little movement Monday on the U.S. Veterans' Day holiday and hesitation ahead of the Fed's meeting, they said. In Argentina, the bolsa is expected to hold steady as investors wait for private pension fund cash flows to pick up towards the end of the week.
"The market will probably stay rangebound for a little while, but the medium-term outlook is good," said Miguel Daneri at Boston Securities.
If New York manages to maintain its bullish tone this week, the Buenos Aires bolsa should digest any selling and consolidate at these levels, said dealers.
The blue-chip MerVal index firmed 0.9 percent last week to 579.36 points and stands 1.5 percent higher so far in November.
The Caracas bolsa ended Friday down 1.3 percent at 5,838.73 points after a mixed week with investors selling shares to raise cash for the offering.
Brazilian stocks are expected to be soft early in the week on concern over the country's widening trade gap, projected to grow as much as $1 billion in October.
The trade data is expected to be released late this week.

Investors will also be following developments in the foreign exchange markets following speculation that the government could speed up the depreciation of the real or tighten monetary policy to close the trade gap, said dealers.
Although the central bank again denied any forex policy change today, traders cited other instances when the central bank has said one thing but done another.
Brazil shares dropped 1.23 percent last week to close at 65,595 points Friday.
Chilean shares are also seen weaker with little news expected that could give stocks a boost, said dealers.
"The market is slumbering this week as there's nothing positive out there for investors," said Lance Eckel, an analyst at brokerage Sud Americano.
The bolsa is expected to be continued to be dragged down by falls in the heavyweight forestry and electricity sectors, said dealers.
Santiago's blue-chip IPSA index ended off 1.74 percent last week at 96.91 points.
Mexican shares are seen angling higher in coming days, provided there are no surprises in municipal and legislative elections held this weekend in three states, said dealers.
Recent weakness is expected to attract foreign investors, who are betting that the Mexican economy will pick up next year, they said.
Mexican stocks rose 2.82 percent, or 91.84 points, in the first seven sessions of the month.
